doc.title: Mrs. P. Thomas Agnes Brown Interview, 1960-10-12

title: 1921-22 Tom Brown's Syncopated Novelty Orchestra at Vista Garden
summary: A Christmas postcard for the orchestra at Vista Garden, with the personnel (Earl Corder, Abe Friedman, Charles Hawk, Ted Brown, George Lee and others).

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: We've got it on tape. Now, here's a, looks like an advertisement. Well, it's a postcard, actually. And it says on it, 1921-1922. Season greetings. A Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year. Compliments of Tom Brown's syncopated novelty orchestra. Now playing unlimited engagement at Vista Garden. It's got a picture of a band. Looks like you've got a band show.
Oh, that's Steve in the background on the band.

And Tom is there with a trombone. There's a cornet player, piano player, clarinetist, and a saxophonist. And they have two more saxophones right in front of the trombone and trumpet. Looks like one's an alto and one's a tenor.
See, Tom played big bands plus small bands. And he's got pictures. My God.

Drummer in the background, too. Tom Brown, director, phonograph artist, and composer of Rosa Spain, June, High Yellow Blues, Love Dreams, and others. Earl Corder drums, Abe Friedman piano. Charles Hawk banjo, Ted Brown bass. George Lee saxophone. Joe Caliguri, C-A-L-I-G-U-R-I, cornet. Roy Kramer. That's K-R-E-A-M-E-R.
Tom Brown syncopated novelty orchestra. And Earl Corder did this. He dated it 1921. He must have done the drawing. He signed it.
Yes, uh-huh. It was between 21, I guess, and 22. He was a drummer.
And he was a drummer and an artist, too. And a drummer.
